lessons.title: ICT, Computer, Data and Information
lessons.notes_html:
ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology. It is a connected system of interactive tools and technologies used to send and receive information, with a focus on communication technology.

The Computer

A computer is an electronic machine that can accept data (input), manipulate the data according to specified rules (process), produce results (output) and store the results for future use.

Data and Information

DataInformation
A collection of raw facts and figures. It is unorganized and not useful by itself. It can be words, numbers, images and sounds.Organized, useful data. It is how you understand the facts, and it is the result of data processing.

So, processed data is called information, and a set of instructions that tells the computer what to do is called a program.

Key Points

  • ICT means Information and Communication Technology.
  • A computer works in four steps: input, process, output and store.
  • Data is raw and unorganized; information is organized and useful.

lessons.title: Input Devices
lessons.notes_html:
An input device allows a user to enter data and commands into the memory of a computer.

Common Input Devices

  • Keyboard — used to type text and commands. The standard keyboard is also called the QWERTY keyboard.
  • Mouse — an input device that looks like a mouse. It has two buttons, left click and right click. Right click displays a pop-up menu with various options.
  • Microphone — used to record audio and voice calls.
  • Digital camera — takes pictures and sends them into the computer.
  • Scanner — scans documents such as photographs, pages of text and books, and converts them into digital format.
  • Biometric sensor — identifies the unique physical characteristics of a person, for example by face, palm, fingerprint or retina and iris scan.

Scanner and Biometric Sensor

A scanner works on documents and books. A biometric sensor works on the body of a person, such as a fingerprint or a face.

Key Points

  • Input devices enter data and commands into the computer.
  • The printer is NOT an input device.
  • A biometric sensor identifies a person by unique physical characteristics.

lessons.title: Hardware, Software and Memory
lessons.notes_html:
Hardware means the physical parts of the computer system that can be seen and touched. Software is a set of instructions (a program) that tells the hardware how to do a job. Hardware cannot perform any task without software, and software cannot be executed without hardware.

RAM and ROM

RAMROM
Random Access Memory. Volatile and temporary: contents are lost when the computer is switched off. Reading and writing are both possible. It is fast.Read Only Memory. Non-volatile and permanent: contents are retained even when the device is powered off. The user can only read it. It is slower and cheaper than RAM.

Storage and Other Parts

  • Motherboard — the main circuit board inside the system unit.
  • USB — Universal Serial Bus, used to connect devices.
  • SSD — Solid State Drive, a secondary storage device that accesses data faster than an HDD and keeps data even without power.

Key Points

  • Hardware can be seen and touched; software is a set of instructions.
  • RAM is temporary and volatile; ROM is permanent and non-volatile.
  • An SSD is faster than an HDD.

lessons.title: Generations of Computers
lessons.notes_html:
Computer development is classified into five generations. In every generation, computers became smaller, faster and more reliable.

GenerationPeriodMain technology
First1940 to 1956Vacuum tubes for circuitry and magnetic drum for memory. UNIVAC and ENIAC are examples.
Second1956 to 1963Transistors replaced vacuum tubes. These computers generated less heat.
Third1964 to 1971Integrated circuits (IC) and semi-conductors were used for the first time. Smaller and more reliable.
Fourth1971 to 1985The microprocessor was used, with thousands of integrated circuits on one chip.
Fifth1985 to present and futureBelongs to Artificial Intelligence, with new technologies like speech recognition.

Key Points

  • First generation used vacuum tubes; second used transistors.
  • Integrated circuits were first used in the third generation.
  • The fifth generation is the age of Artificial Intelligence.

lessons.title: The Keyboard and the Modem
lessons.notes_html:
The standard keyboard is called the QWERTY keyboard, after the first letters of its top letter row. It has four main segments.

Segments of the Keyboard

  • Function keys — the 12 keys marked F1 to F12 at the top. Every function key has a different meaning in different software, but F1 is used for HELP in almost all software.
  • Typewriter keys — the main block of letter keys.
  • Cursor control keys — the arrow keys that move the cursor.
  • Numeric keypad — the block on the right side for quick number entry. It has digits 0 to 9, plus / * + - . Num Lock and Enter.

The Modem

A modem is a communications device that enables computers to communicate via telephone lines, so users can exchange data and information with another computer.

Key Points

  • F1 to F12 are function keys; F1 gives help in almost all software.
  • The numeric pad is used for quick number entry.
  • A modem connects computers through telephone lines.

lessons.title: What Is an Operating System?
lessons.notes_html:
An operating system (OS) is system software that manages the hardware of the computer. It manages the computer memory and processes, as well as all of its hardware and software, and it allows you to communicate with the computer.

Why a Computer Needs an OS

Without an operating system, a computer cannot do anything: no program can run and no hardware can be used. The OS is the link between the user, the programs and the hardware.

Microsoft Windows

  • Windows is an operating system designed by Microsoft.
  • It allows you to use a computer through a graphical interface.
  • It is the most popular operating system for home computers.
  • The book names Windows 11 as the newest version.

Key Points

  • An operating system is system software that manages hardware, memory and processes.
  • Windows is designed by Microsoft, not by Apple.
  • Without an OS, a computer cannot work at all.

The Windows Desktop is the main screen of the operating system. On it you have access to tools like the Start Menu, the Taskbar and other icons.

Desktop Icons

Desktop icons are small images that represent programs, files and folders. Their purpose is to give quick access to frequently used programs, files and folders.

This PC and Recycle Bin

  • This PC — the new name of My Computer in Windows 10. It shows different icons like documents, downloads, music, videos, hard drives, CD and USB.
  • Recycle Bin — a special folder where deleted items are temporarily stored. Deleted files are not permanently removed, and files in the Recycle Bin can be restored to their original location.

Key Points

  • The Desktop is the main screen of the operating system.
  • Icons are small images for programs, files and folders.
  • Deleted items go to the Recycle Bin and can be restored.

lessons.title: Files and Folders
lessons.notes_html:
A file is a collection of data or information stored in a computer. A folder is a container that contains files or other folders, called subfolders, or both.

Why We Need Folders

Folders let us organize our files so they can be stored, found and managed easily, instead of lying mixed together.

Making a File and a Folder

  • To make a file: double-click This PC, click Documents, open your folder, right-click in the empty area, select New, then Text Document, and rename it.
  • To create a folder on the Desktop: right-click on an empty part of the Desktop, select New, then click Folder, and type a name.
  • Shortcut for a new folder in File Explorer: Ctrl + Shift + N.

Key Points

  • A file stores data; a folder is a container for files and subfolders.
  • Folders keep work organized and easy to find.
  • Ctrl + Shift + N creates a new folder.

Windows gives simple tools to move, copy and remove files and folders.

CopyCut
Reproduces a file or folder without removing the original. Shortcut: Ctrl + C, then Paste with Ctrl + V.Moves a file or folder: the original is removed from its first location once it is pasted at the new location. Shortcut: Ctrl + X, then Paste with Ctrl + V.

Deleting and Dragging

  • To delete: select the file or folder, right-click and choose Delete, or use the Delete button in the Ribbon. Click Yes in the confirmation window. The item goes to the Recycle Bin.
  • Dragging means moving the mouse while keeping the mouse button pushed down over a file or folder, moving it to a new location, and then lifting the button to drop it there.

Key Points

  • Ctrl + C copies, Ctrl + V pastes, Ctrl + X cuts.
  • Copy keeps the original; Cut removes it after pasting.
  • Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin first.

lessons.title: What Is the Internet?
lessons.notes_html:
The Internet, also called the Net, is a global network of billions of computers and other electronic devices. It is the largest network in the world: a network of networks made up of millions of private, public, business and government networks.

History in Short

  • ARPANET stands for Advanced Research Projects Agency Network, an early network.
  • NSF stands for National Science Foundation.
  • Networks are connected by physical cables (copper telephone wires, TV cables and fiber optic cables) and by wireless connections like Wi-Fi and 3G/4G.

Getting Connected: ISP

ISP stands for Internet Service Provider. The type of service you get depends on your ISP: dial-up (slowest, uses a phone line), DSL (broadband, much faster than dial-up), cable (via cable TV), satellite (through satellites) and 3G/4G (wireless, mostly for mobile phones). DSL service uses a broadband connection.

Key Points

  • The Internet is a global network of networks.
  • An ISP provides your internet connection.
  • Dial-up is the slowest type; DSL is broadband.

A problem is a situation or an issue that needs to be solved.

Steps of Problem Solving

  • Identifying the problem — figuring out what the problem is: what is going wrong or what needs to be fixed. Example: you cannot find your favourite book.
  • Gather information about the problem.
  • Think of solutions (brainstorming).
  • Evaluate the solutions and choose the best one.
  • Implement the chosen solution.
  • Check if it worked, and learn from the experience (reflecting).

Key Points

  • A problem is a situation that needs to be solved.
  • Simple problems are easy; complex problems have many parts.

lessons.title: What Is an Algorithm?
lessons.notes_html:
An algorithm is a set of clear, step-by-step instructions that help you solve a problem or complete a task. In short, it is a set of rules to be followed. Step-by-step presentation of the solution of a problem is called an algorithm.

Origin of the Word

The word algorithm is derived from the name of the mathematician Mohammed ibn-Musa al-Khwarizmi (born 780 AD in Iraq; died 850 AD).

First and Last Steps

  • The first step of every algorithm is Start.
  • The last step of every algorithm is End.
  • Between Start and End, each step must be written in the right order.

Writing an algorithm means creating a step-by-step procedure or set of rules to solve a specific problem or perform a task, before any coding is done.

Key Points

  • An algorithm is a step-by-step set of rules to solve a problem.
  • Its name comes from the mathematician al-Khwarizmi.
  • Every algorithm begins with Start and finishes with End.

lessons.notes_html:
A program is a set of well-defined instructions given to the computer to do a task. Code is a set of logical, mathematical and sequential instructions.

The Compiler

A compiler is a special program that translates code written in a high-level programming language into machine code, which the computer hardware can directly execute. It works in three steps:

  • Source code — the programmer writes code in a high-level language like C++, Java or C#.
  • Compilation — the compiler checks the source code for errors and converts it into machine code or an intermediate code.
  • Output — the result is usually an executable file, like .exe on Windows, that the computer can run.

Key Points

  • A program is a set of instructions for doing a task.
  • A compiler converts a high level language program into machine language.
  • A compiler does NOT convert a middle language program into a high level language.

CopyrightA law that helps protect creative works and ideas. If you create something original, like a drawing, a story or a song, you have the right to decide how others can use it. It gives creators exclusive rights to use and distribute their creations.
PlagiarismUsing someone else's work, ideas or expressions without proper acknowledgment, presenting them as your own.
PiracyThe unauthorized use, distribution or reproduction of copyrighted materials, such as music, movies, software or books, without permission from the copyright holder.

Avoiding Plagiarism

Copying text without credit, paraphrasing ideas without citing the source, and submitting someone else's work as your own are all plagiarism. It can lead to academic penalties, loss of credibility, legal consequences and damage to reputation. Avoid it by giving credit, using your own words, and citing sources. Piracy is illegal and unethical because it deprives creators of revenue and recognition.

  • Plagiarism is passing off another person's work as your own.

Entrepreneurship is the process of starting and running a new business or venture.

Digital Entrepreneurship

Digital entrepreneurship is the process of creating and managing a business primarily online, using digital technologies and the internet to deliver products or services. In short, it is the smart application of the power of digital technologies to business.

  • Digital entrepreneurs use websites, social media, e-commerce and mobile apps to reach customers, market their offerings and operate their businesses.
  • Its three principal components are the vision, the technology and the strategy.
  • A manufacturer utilizes raw materials to create products that are then sold in the market.
  • Famous founders: Facebook was created by Mark Zuckerberg, Uber was introduced by Travis Kalanick, Alibaba was founded by Jack Ma, and Jingdong (JD.com) was founded by Richard Liu in 1998.

Key Points

  • Digital entrepreneurship runs the business primarily online.

lessons.title: The Entrepreneurship Process and Amazon's Story
lessons.notes_html:
The entrepreneurship process, how to start a business, has six steps.

Six Steps

  • 1. Idea Generation — come up with a new idea for a product or service that solves a problem, makes life easier, or is just fun. This is the first step.
  • 2. Research — learn more: Will people like this? Is anyone else doing this?
  • 3. Planning — make a plan like a roadmap: how the business will work, what you need, and how much money it will cost.
  • 4. Start the Business — put the plan into action, create the product or service and start selling it.
  • 5. Manage and Grow — keep customers happy, keep track of money, and make the business better.
  • 6. Evaluate and Improve — check how the business is going, fix what is not working, and keep improving.

How Amazon Started

Amazon started as a small online bookstore in 1994. It was created by Jeff Bezos, who began in his garage in Seattle, Washington, to sell books all over the world using the internet. It became popular because buying books online was easy. Then Amazon added music, movies, electronics and toys, and today it is known for fast shipping and a wide selection.

Key Points

  • Idea Generation is the first step of the entrepreneurship process.
  • A plan works like a roadmap for the business.
  • Amazon began in 1994 as an online bookstore in a garage.
